newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: ING denies rift with Dillon Read.
newsitem.headline: ING denies rift with Dillon Read.

text.p: ING Groep NV Friday denied newspaper reports of a dispute with Dillon Read & Co. over ING's interest in buying the remaining 75 percent of the U.S. investment bank that it does not already own.
"There's no disagreement. This is part of the game," Ruud Polet, a spokesman for the Dutch financial services group, said.
The Financial Times said Dillon Read was resisting attempts by ING Barings, ING's London-based investment banking arm, to boost its current stockholding of 25 percent.
Referring to the Financial Times report, Polet said it did not say Dillon Read "does not like us," adding that the relationship between the two groups remained good.
ING said Thursday it was interested in buying the remaining 75 percent of the privately-held Wall Street firm under the right conditions.
They are in talks, expected to last for several weeks, for ING to buy the balance outstanding or sell its shareholding to the partners of Dillon Read.
The partners have an option to buy back the ING Barings stake before July 1.
